newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE UP AMID CASH SHORTAGE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE UP AMID CASH SHORTAGE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market edged up on Tuesday in response to what dealers said was a temporary cash shortage in the system.
"The market is a bit short. There are no maturities from today until Friday so we've raised the rates a bit," a dealer said.
However, he said that the shortage of cash would be shortlived. "But it's just a temporary shortage for this week only. Rates should be coming back down next week."
Traders said the rise in inflation to 16.4 percent from 13.1 percent announced on Monday was not significant enough to affect local money rates.
"If it had gone to, say, 20 percent then we would have seen some movement," the dealer said.
On Tuesday, discount houses were selling treasury bills at 17.85 percent, up from 17.80 percent on Monday.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were also quoted firmer at 20.50 and 19.50 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 19.50 and 18.25 percent. Bankers acceptances were at 18.50 and 17.85 percent from 18.15 and 17.80 percent. Call money went up to 18.5 percent from Monday's 17 percent.
Figures from the Reserve Bank, however, indicated a surplus of Z$336.8 million at the close of Monday trade.
